analysis.title: Fed, BoC and UK budget: a busy day for markets
key_insights: The Fed and BoC announce policy decisions on 28 October 2026, with the ECB and BoE following Thursday. The Fed is expected to hold rates at 3.75%-4.00%, and markets will focus on Chair Kevin Warsh's remarks.
The 10-year US Treasury yield is around 5%. A more hawkish-than-expected Warsh speech could push it well above that level.
The market is pricing a 20bp BoC rate hike, the first in more than three years, reflecting Governor Macklem's concerns about inflation driven by rising energy prices.
The UK budget is presented Wednesday. Gilts yield 5.34%, sterling trades at $1.3313, and markets expect restrictive fiscal policy.
AI-related company earnings are currently driving equity market moves and are being watched ahead of the Fed decision.

EUR rates: MNI reports on ECB deliberations suggest higher yields and tighter financial conditions could give the ECB more time to assess inflation, making a December hike less certain. Markets still price an 80% probability of a December hike.
The 10Y Bund yield held around 3.35-3.40% while the 2Y Schatz fell 2 bps. The 10Y OAT-Bund spread widened 3 bps to 156 bps after weak French consumer confidence.
The dollar rose against all G10 currencies, with EUR/USD down 0.26% to 1.1143. AUD and NZD were the best G10 performers on the tech rebound and improved risk appetite.
Credit: iTraxx Main fell 2 bps, iTraxx Xover fell 12 bps and CDX IG fell 1 bp as tech newsflow calmed markets. Oracle CDS fell 10 bps, SpaceX 8 bps and Meta 6 bps.
Credit calendar this week: 17 banks, six carmakers, four technology companies and three utilities report results. Non-financial primary issuance exceeds €5bn, almost two-thirds of it from P&G.
France: consumer confidence fell to a historic low of 80 in October from 85 in September, a level seen only once in 20 years, pointing to weak household consumption.
Euro area: the ECB bank lending survey shows mortgage credit demand collapsed (-27% net in Q3 vs -12% expected) on rising rates, lower consumer confidence and a weaker housing outlook.
US data: Conference Board consumer confidence surged to 91.7 in October vs 81.0 expected. Durable goods orders rose 1.8% in September vs 1.7% expected. New home sales fell 0.6% m/m.
Mercedes-Benz cut FY2026 EBIT and Industrial FCF guidance on China weakness and raw-material cost inflation, raising questions about next year's margin recovery for European autos.

HSBC Q3 2026: top-line miss offset by cost discipline and better credit provisions, bottom line broadly in line. Natixis flags softening NII momentum from deposit competition and higher pass-through beta in Hong Kong.
earnings_insights: HSBC Q3 2026 (reported): revenue missed consensus, offset by lower costs and better-than-expected credit provisions, leaving the bottom line broadly in line with consensus. NII momentum is softening.
Mercedes-Benz Group preliminary results (reported 27 Oct 2026): Industrial FCF fell short of expectations. FY2026 EBIT and Industrial FCF guidance was cut. Full results due 28 Oct.
This week's results: 17 banks, six carmakers, four technology companies and three utilities.

A first hike in over three years, driven by energy-led inflation concerns.
Probability remains high, though MNI reports suggest less certainty.
Historic low, signalling continued weak household consumption.
Employment growth slowed to 2.1% y/y from 2.3%.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Mortgage demand collapsed on rising rates and a weaker housing outlook. Business loans +4.2% and household loans +3.1% in September.

risk_factors: A more hawkish-than-expected Warsh speech could push the 10Y UST yield well above 5%.
Restrictive UK fiscal policy at the budget, with gilts at 5.34%.
Bond market stress and rising yields are weighing on euro area mortgage demand and consumer confidence.
Mercedes-Benz guidance cut on China weakness and raw-material cost inflation may hit the broader European auto margin recovery.
Calm in credit after the tech newsflow may be temporary.
vol_and_positioning: VIX futures at 19.1, down 0.2 points on the day and up 2.2 points over five days.
iTraxx Europe Main 5Y at 65bp (-2.2), Crossover at 322bp (-11.9), Financial Senior at 74bp (-2.6).
geopolitical: Engie and the Belgian State are negotiating over acquisition of Engie's Belgian nuclear operations. Heads of Terms target is 4 November 2026, and the government has drafted legislation enabling compulsory acquisition if talks fail.
